The widening of the 90% confidence intervals across the horizons directly reflects the increasing uncertainty associated with predicting outcomes further into the future. While my forecasts aim to capture the most probable outcomes, several specific risks or events could push the actual value outside these stated intervals. Conversely, a major positive economic surprise, a breakthrough innovation, unexpectedly strong earnings or market performance, or a swift resolution of global tensions could drive the value significantly above the upper bounds. These "tail risks" are less likely but could dramatically alter the trajectory of the value, placing it beyond the 90% confidence range.
